findings.premise: The design distinguishes observation failure from actual provider completion and specifies retryable handling.
findings.evidence: Adapter resume currently converts ordinary read failures into error events and returns normally for SegmentGone. Lifecycle follow treats both normal exits as ended and clears the cursor; only a thrown exception yields failed. The proposed observation-failure boundary directly addresses this mismatch and explicitly retains cursor/status on read failure. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/cli-adapter.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/turn-lifecycle.ts, docs/standalone/multiple-concurrent-chats-chat-panel-active-E202611031bd72813/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Retain tests proving that ordinary read failures and missing segments cannot masquerade as successful observation of completion.

findings.premise: Decision-delivery failures are detectable under the proposed transport changes, including restored processes without writable stdin.
findings.evidence: Current decide() consumes the pending request before checking live stdin and returns void; nodeSpawner.write swallows synchronous write failures. A resumed TurnProcess exposes stop/kill but no write transport. The design explicitly adds delivery results, durable native-session capture, stop-and-verify recovery, and delivery-failed/session-lost outcomes rather than assuming a resumed process is writable. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/cli-adapter.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/turn-lifecycle.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts]
findings.action: Implement delivery results through the actual stdin completion/error path and retain the proposed reload, dead-stdin and first-turn recovery tests.

summary.prose: The chat panel tab header gains a second dropdown next to the history control listing active chats — agent working (yellow) or waiting for user input (red), plus done chats (green) until purged from the list after 30 minutes of inactivity. Status is extension-local, derived from the turn lifecycle and stream events, persisted in the existing session store (with per-chat pendingRequests retained by requestId + resolution state), and reconciled for detached sessions by a 60 s observer grounded in LiveTurn + session-output + pid liveness; selecting an entry posts the existing open-chat { chatId } message, exactly like the history dropdown. History is untouched. Separately, every insrc_present declaration opens the artifact in a NEW presentation/editor panel (panel key = presentKey = artifactId#hostPresentSeq) instead of replacing the content of the already-open panel — the presentation panel component itself is unchanged; only its multiplicity changes.

api.name: session-store status tracking

uxDefinition.narrative: Two component mocks for the concurrent-chats story, based on the current webview UX: (1) the full chat panel webview as it is today (.box > .chrome / #insrc-term / #insrc-progress / .inputbar / .statusbar), with the new #insrc-active chip LEFT-aligned in .chrome (red/yellow/green status-dot entries) and the unchanged #insrc-history chip RIGHT-aligned in .right.

body.description: Component mock 1 — the whole chat webview panel as it is today (renderShell, chat-panel.ts:1545): body.insrc-term > .box fills the editor pane edge-to-edge as a flex column — .chrome header, #insrc-older pager, #insrc-term scrolling transcript (the only scroll region), #insrc-progress live band, .inputbar (❯ send/stop + 2-line textarea), .statusbar (attach, edits mode, bottom-right run controls). The ONLY addition is the active-chats dropdown chip LEFT-aligned in .chrome; #insrc-history stays as the sole RIGHT-aligned chip (.right, margin-left:auto).
